chapter: Buck and Bubbles: Nazarro and Bubbles
title: Singing Rhythm For Sale and shifting toward Bubbles' rhythm tap
summary: The boys sang the theme and tapped their Shorty and Slim number, but Green's style changed once he fell for Bubbles' rhythm tap.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: They would sing the song and then you would come out and tap to it.
They already sang it, but we come out there and they had us, instead of us doing "Sweet Sue", they had us to do -- repeat the "Rhythm For Sale" song, you see.
What sort of tap went along with it?
Well, the Short and Slim tap dance we was doing. That was the only tap dance we knew at that time, you know.
Can you tap part of it?
Well, I don't actually remember the entire routine, because my style of tap dancing changed so tremendously. Like I was taking a Ride the Horse and so forth, a few steps

that J.D. taught me. I stopped doing them, you see, because my style changed tap dancing. Actually I fell in love with the way John W. Bubbles, you know, his style of tap dancing. It was rhythm tap. It was becoming popular then, you see.
Did you feel that John Bubbles' type of tap was much more sophisticated, much --

-- more advanced, and you had already learned the other forms of tap, and up to that point they were sort of novelty sort of forms. But now you felt as if you had -- you were starting to -- your mind was starting to think in terms of more complex sort of rhythms.
